text: What is David Lewis's problem of temporary intrinsics?
choices: The puzzle of how one persisting object can have incompatible intrinsic properties (e.g., being straight, then bent) at different times without instantiating contradictory properties
The puzzle of how two numerically distinct ships can be built from exactly the same planks arranged in the same way
The puzzle of how the self can be a genuine unity when introspection reveals only a succession of distinct perceptions
The puzzle of how psychological continuity can hold between one earlier person and two distinct later persons
explanation: The problem of temporary intrinsics is that one and the same persisting object seems to instantiate incompatible intrinsic properties (straight at one time, bent at another), which threatens contradiction because a single thing cannot have contradictory properties. The reassembled-ship option is the Ship of Theseus (material-identity) puzzle, the succession-of-perceptions option is Hume's problem of the unity of the bundle, and the one-earlier-to-two-later option is the fission/reduplication problem — each a distinct puzzle from this unit.
